approachQuestion.prompt:
Calibration Log
A non-rewindable stream delivers n signed integers. After each arrival, emit the lower median of the prefix: the value at one-based rank ceil(prefixLength/2) in sorted order, counting duplicates. Example: [8,2,5,1] → [8,2,5,2].

1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; values fit signed 32 bits. Read the stream once; emitted values cannot later be read as workspace. Which approach best meets this contract?
constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 200000; values fit signed 32 bits. Read the stream once; emitted values cannot later be read as workspace.

options.text: Keep a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half. Insert each arrival on the appropriate side, then rebalance so the lower half has the same size as the upper half or one extra value. Emit the lower root.
options.feedback: The ordering boundary separates all lower values from all upper values; the size invariant makes the lower root the required rank, including duplicates.

options.text: Keep arrivals in a sorted dynamic array, shifting entries on insertion, and emit its required middle entry.
options.feedback: The rank is correct, but repeatedly shifting a growing sorted prefix is avoidable.

options.text: Keep only the smallest and largest values seen; emit their average rounded down.
options.feedback: For [1,2,100], the median is 2 while this average is 50.

options.text: Keep the lower half in a min-heap and emit its root.
options.feedback: The lower half needs its largest value. For [1,2,3,4], the lower median is 2 rather than 1.

details: Keep a max-heap for the lower half and a min-heap for the upper half. Insert each arrival on the appropriate side, then rebalance so the lower half has the same size as the upper half or one extra value. Emit the lower root.

All lower-heap values must stay no greater than upper-heap values. Size balance makes the lower root the requested lower median. Maintaining only two heap sizes without the value-order invariant cannot identify a median.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze A with two array-backed binary heaps and a constant number of heap transfers per arrival. Let n be total arrivals. Output uses a separate append-only sink; heap buffer growth is amortized over the full stream. Choose the tightest time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use the tightest worst-case bound for the whole input unless amortized or expected accounting is explicitly specified. Comparing or moving a record and arithmetic on machine words take constant time.

Exclude supplied input and returned output from auxiliary space. Count working arrays, queues, tables and call stacks. Output storage is separate and is not used as workspace. Heap repairs and traversals are iterative. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(n log(n+1)) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(n log(n+1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each arrival causes logarithmic repairs while both heaps retain all readings.
details: Each arrival can require logarithmic heap repairs; adverse sequences attain that cost on a linear fraction of arrivals. The two heaps retain n observations. Output emission costs linear time but output space is excluded. Amortized array growth is linear overall.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Heap insertion and rebalancing are not constant-time in the worst case.
“O(n log(n+1)) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The heaps retain the complete prefix even though only one rank is emitted.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This describes repeated array shifting, not heap repair paths.
